analysis.title: Who is buying all the hyperscaler bonds?
key_insights: JPM counts $232bn of hyperscaler issuance and $42bn of datacenter issuance in USD HG YTD, up 160% y/y. Investors worry about demand because issuance is not expected to slow next year.

8 insurers with $1.8tr of General Account assets disclosed AI exposure for the first time this quarter. JPM estimates AI-related assets at about 2.27% of their asset base, versus 6.87% that AI issuers represent in the JULI HG index.

For the roughly 45% of hyperscaler par with holder data ($193bn of $443bn in JULI), insurers own about 25% of the 6 hyperscalers' bonds versus about 45% for the rest of the HG market. Insurance ownership of hyperscalers is lower than in any other HG sector.
Insurers own an estimated 16-17% of data-center bonds. Asset managers hold 53% of hyperscaler bonds and 79% of data-center bonds in the samples with visibility.

ETFs hold 17% of hyperscaler bonds versus 3% of data-center bonds. JPM links this to the 144A-for-life status of data-center bonds, which makes them ineligible for many ETFs that track the Bloomberg Agg. This could change if the index rule consultation changes the rules.
JPM's thesis is 'price creates capacity'. Another $50bn of hyperscaler bonds were issued over the past two weeks as hyperscaler spreads hit new cycle wides, and most YTD issuance came at local wides.

Insurer disclosures are about 1%-3% of invested assets, with Corebridge, Athene and Global Atlantic at the higher end. Management teams stressed investment-grade ratings, secured claims, conservative LTVs and lease-backed cash flows, and limited speculative construction and neocloud exposure.

JPM sees the insurer exposure data as showing insurers are keenly aware that each wave of issuance may come at wider spreads, and that wider entry points may still come, particularly in structured, illiquid deals such as GPU financings.

A heavier mix of GPU financings is expected in coming months. A reported $103bn across the two now in motion has weighed on spreads for the broader hyperscaler complex, partly because pricing details emerge to the market after the fact and may imply relative value pressure on senior unsecured hyperscaler bonds.

GPU financings so far all have tenors under 10 years. Spread product from 1 to 10 years totals $21.1tr versus $4.5tr beyond 10 years, so the front end is nearly 5x larger. The greater range of competing products should raise the relative value hurdle for GPU financings.

Cross-product spreads: IG corporates are 71bp at the front end, 89bp at 5yr and 106bp at 10yr, versus ranges of roughly 33-190bp, 28-174bp and 39-542bp across other spread products. At 30yr, munis at 90bp are essentially the only competing spread product versus 121bp for IG corporates.
The hyperscaler 10s30s spread curve is +5bp YTD to 36bp. JPM attributes the long-end underperformance to concentration risk and a lack of alternative long-duration spread products.
Hyperscaler spreads have widened more than the JULI index across tenors since YE25. At 1-3y hyperscalers are 102.6bp vs JULI 72.4bp, and at 10y+ hyperscalers are 172.6bp vs 108.6bp.

Insurance ownership by issuer is highest for Aaa-rated MSFT (45%) and lowest for Baa1-rated SPCX (13%), with about 25% for the other four. ORCL insurance ownership looks high for its rating, which JPM attributes mainly to about 40% of its bonds having been issued when it was A-rated.

JPM concludes insurer AI exposure is not particularly high relative to the market and asset managers have done the bulk of AI bond buying so far. The mix could become more balanced as GPU financings take center stage.

sector_views.rationale: Insurers are underweight hyperscaler and data-center bonds relative to the HG index and to asset managers, so insurance capacity is not currently a constraint on issuance.

earnings_insights: 8 insurers disclosed AI exposure with Q3 2026 results: MET $4.1bn (~1.0% of GA), ATH $12.9bn (~3.1%, deck dated 10/30/26), PRU $7.2bn (~1.8%), CRBG $9.0bn (~3.5%), GBLATL $5.4bn (~3.5%, Sept investor deck), RGA ~2% (about $2.8bn), EQH <2% (about $2.4bn), JXN <2% (about $1.5bn), VOYA ~2% (about $0.8bn). These are company-reported disclosures and JPM estimates, not consensus figures. MET, PRU, RGA, JXN and others reported Q3 on 11/02-11/05/26.

Total disclosed AI exposure across the sample is about $46.3bn on $2,038bn of asset base, or about 2.3% (JPM estimate). Definitions differ across insurers, since some include semiconductors or SPCX and some do not.
risk_factors: Wider spreads on GPU financings, once pricing details emerge, could pressure senior unsecured hyperscaler bonds.
Insurance demand may be needed as issuance volumes stay high and GPU financings grow, and insurers show a preference for wider entry points.
Long-end hyperscaler concentration risk, magnified by the lack of alternative long-duration spread products.
Insurer disclosure is not uniform and covers only a handful of insurers, so exposure comparisons are directional rather than precise.
Index rule changes from the ongoing consultation could alter ETF eligibility for data-center bonds.
charts_described: Figure 1 and 5 compare insurer AI exposure of 2.27% of GA assets with AI-linked bonds at 4.68% of the US HG index (hyperscalers 1.63%, data centers 0.56%).
Figure 2 and 7 show insurance owning 25% of hyperscaler bonds versus 45% of the rest of the US HG index, with asset managers at 53% versus 37% (as read from the text labels).
Figure 16 shows JULI spread by tenor versus hyperscaler spread, for example 1-3y at 72.4bp vs 102.6bp and 10y+ at 108.6bp vs 172.6bp.
vol_and_positioning: Hyperscaler spreads hit new cycle wides over the past two weeks, with the JULI hyperscaler index well above the JULI ex-hyperscaler index.
Hyperscaler 10s30s spread curve is +5bp YTD to 36bp.

Positioning by holder type: hyperscaler bonds are held 53% by asset managers, 25% by insurers and 17% by ETFs. About 25% of the asset manager portion is foreign for hyperscalers, versus 10% for data centers.

tension_points.bull_case: Insurers hold about 2.27% of assets in AI-linked bonds against 6.87% in the JULI HG index and own only about 25% of hyperscaler bonds, so they have room to buy more. Wider spreads create additional capacity ('price creates capacity').
tension_points.bear_case: Insurers are deliberately not leaning in and are waiting for wider entry points. Asset managers have done most of the buying, and GPU financings may need a different, more diversified buyer base.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A shift in the buyer mix as GPU financings take center stage, with pricing details on the $103bn of GPU deals emerging at wider spreads.

theme_stances.key_argument: Insurance capacity is not an issue so far because asset managers are doing the bulk of the buying.
theme_stances.evidence: insurance capacity isn’t an issue so far as asset managers are doing the bulk of buying

theme_stances.key_argument: GPU financings are weighing on spreads for the broader hyperscaler complex and face a wider relative value hurdle because of the larger range of competing products inside 10 years.
theme_stances.evidence: the diversity of product at the front-end should entail a wider relative value hurdle
